findings.statement: CA9 is a known target control with full surface accessibility and good ADC suitability [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647], placed high among all scored genes [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; rank=13]. Vital-organ staining is strong in the stomach [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_staining_level=3] while kidney staining is absent, and the weakest quarter of donors has a limited share of tumour cells expressing it [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3%] (median donor [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_median_donor=53.3%]). The score does not show that a conjugate would work.

CD70 has the second-best ADC suitability score [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746] with full surface accessibility, but staining data are not available, so normal-tissue safety cannot be judged. In the weakest quarter of donors few tumour cells express it [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=17.7%] (median donor [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_median_donor=41.2%]), so heterogeneous expression is a limit.

SCARB1 ranks first in the target profile but its ADC suitability is lower [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.558]. Staining is strong in the adrenal gland [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_staining_level=3] and moderate in kidney [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=2], and very few tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%] (median donor [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_median_donor=12.4%]), which argues against a simple conjugate or radioligand.

ENPP3, a known target control, has moderate ADC suitability [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578]. Staining is strong in the duodenum [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_staining_level=3] and in kidney [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3], and a limited share of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=21.3%]; kidney and gut staining are safety concerns.

In IMmotion150, higher CA9 expression is associated with longer benefit in the atezolizumab plus bevacizumab arm [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.112] [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.665] and in the sunitinib arm, but the difference between arms is not significant [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.779]. These are leads only, not prediction.

Higher CD70 is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab in IMmotion150 [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.383], the strongest of its arms, but it is not significant after correction [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.166] and the difference between arms is null [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.927].

Higher PSAT1 points towards earlier progression in the atezolizumab arm [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab.log_hr_per_sd=0.164] [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab.padj=0.829] and in the small nivolumab trial (direction only); neither is significant, so it is an unproven lead.

For NNMT only the small nivolumab cohort is reported [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_choueiri2016.n=16], with earlier progression at higher expression (direction only, [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_choueiri2016.padj=0.782]); no IMmotion150 arm result is available, so the treatment layer says almost nothing.

EPAS1 has only the small nivolumab result [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_choueiri2016.n=16], with longer benefit at higher expression (direction only, [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_choueiri2016.padj=0.88]); it cannot support any treatment-response claim.

CA9 is flagged as a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1 mutation: the mutant minus wild-type difference is positive in CPTAC RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971] [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.padj=0.014] and in TCGA RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148], though the CPTAC protein difference is only suggestive [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_protein.padj=0.067]. It is also below ccA levels in ccB tumours in TCGA RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-1.551].

PSAT1 is above ccA levels in ccB tumours in CPTAC protein [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.cptac_protein.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=0.541] and TCGA RNA [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=2.364], and above wild-type in BAP1-mutant tumours in TCGA RNA [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711] but not in protein [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.cptac_protein.padj=0.396], so it is not flagged as a subgroup target candidate.

PCK1 is not a subgroup target candidate for any of VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2. It falls in ccB relative to ccA in TCGA RNA [gene=PCK1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-2.581] but not in protein [gene=PCK1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.cptac_protein.padj=0.898], so it tracks the ccA/ccB split at RNA level rather than a mutation.

EPAS1 is one of the genes that define the ccA/ccB split and falls in ccB tumours [gene=EPAS1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-0.935]. It is not a subgroup target candidate for any mutation.

CD70 is not a checkpoint control, but a large part of its tumour transcripts are attributed to immune cells [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654], and it correlates with CD8 T cells [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_cd8_t_cells=0.278] and regulatory T cells [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_regulatory_t_cells=0.228]. Its tumour signal is therefore partly infiltrate-driven.

FCGR3A is almost entirely immune [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] and tracks the overall immune score [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.795]. It marks hot, infiltrated tumours and is a control, not a tumour-cell conjugate target.

NNMT is attributed to tumour cells in both single-cell datasets, with a high tumour-cell share in Li 2022 [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.97] and in Zhang 2021 [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.948], and tumour cells are far above proximal tubule in both. Zhang 2021 has few paired donors [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_paired_donors=4].

SCARB1 attribution does not hold: the dominant group is myeloid in Li 2022 [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336] but RCC in Zhang 2021 [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582]. Tumour-cell expression is therefore uncertain.

PSAT1 attribution disagrees between datasets: T/NK cells dominate in Li 2022 [gene=PSAT1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.072] versus RCC in Zhang 2021 [gene=PSAT1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.78]. Tumour cells are below proximal tubule in both datasets.

CA9 is called RCC in both single-cell datasets, Li 2022 [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.976] and Zhang 2021 [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.981], with tumour cells far above tubule in both; this is the most consistent attribution among the candidates checked.

SCARB1 protein replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334] [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.28e-10], in a modest number of pairs [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_pairs=33].

NNMT protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776] [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.07e-46]; fold-change size differs by technology and should not be compared with discovery.

The PSAT1 protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946], but its one phosphosite measured in both cohorts does not replicate [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); phosphosites_replicating=0].

The PCK1 protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819], and both phosphosites measured in both cohorts replicate [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); phosphosites_replicating=2].

The HK2 protein increase seen in discovery [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_discovery_log2fc=2.106] does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074], which weakens HK2 as a candidate.

caveats: CA9 and CD70 were not tested in the confirmatory cohort (fewer than 10 matched tumour-normal pairs); this is not a failure to replicate.

No gene differs between the atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and sunitinib arms after correction; all treatment findings are associations from single arms of about 90 patients or a 16-patient trial and are leads only.
ADC suitability scores do not show that a conjugate or radioligand would work; CD70 has no staining data.
SLC16A3 and ENPP3 treatment results, and SLC16A3, PSAT1 and PCK1 ADC and immune layers, were not all queried within the call budget.
Immune genes can differ between subgroups only through infiltration.
